citation: Song, M., Wayne, A. J., Garet, M. S., Brown, S., & Rickles, J. (2021). Impact of providing teachers and principals with performance feedback on their practice and student achievement: Evidence from a large-scale randomized experiment. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 14(2), 353-378. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2020.1868030 [Underlying study and impact estimates extracted from the open-access IES/NCEE final report: Garet, M. S., Wayne, A. J., Brown, S., Rickles, J., Song, M., & Manzeske, D. (2017). The Impact of Providing Performance Feedback to Teachers and Principals (NCEE 2018-4001). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.]
design: Cluster RCT; schools randomly assigned (within district random-assignment blocks) to treatment vs business-as-usual control in 8 districts; 63 treatment + 64 control = 127 schools (126 in Year 2 analyses); regular elementary and middle schools; outcome = grade 4-8 student achievement in reading/ELA and mathematics on state achievement tests (district administrative records); registry grade band = Mixed (elementary + middle). Intervention = providing teachers and principals with performance feedback (classroom-observation ratings via CLASS or FFT, value-added student-growth reports, and a 360-degree principal-leadership survey) over two school years (2012-13 and 2013-14).
problems: The meta-analysis cites the journal article 'Song et al. 2021' (Song first author), which is closed access (Taylor & Francis; OpenAlex/Unpaywall both report is_oa=false, no OA location). The journal article reports the SAME large-scale randomized experiment as the open-access IES/NCEE final report (NCEE 2018-4001, ERIC ED578873, AIR authors with Song as a co-author). Numbers were extracted from the legal open-access NCEE final report (verified PDF, 6.1 MB). Impact estimates, SEs, and p-values are taken from Exhibit J.26 (overall covariate-adjusted three-level HLM model). The achievement outcomes are district-standardized z-scores reported in student-level SD units, so the 'Estimated difference' IS the standardized impact (d in SD units) and the 'Standard error' is in the same SD units; group means are standardized (within-group SD = 1.0, not separately reported). The report does not tabulate an ICC; left null (never guessed). n_t/n_c are student counts; n_clusters = number of schools. The report gives effect-size figures (Exhibit 3.12) as graphics; numeric values taken from Exhibit J.26.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Performance feedback to teachers and principals (classroom-observation ratings + value-added student-growth reports + 360-degree principal-leadership survey) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: State mathematics achievement test (district administrative records, standardized to student-level SD units within district/grade/subject)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post Year 2 (spring 2014, cumulative two-year end-of-treatment wave)
effect_sizes.g_method: Outcome scores reported in student-level SD units; estimated difference from three-level HLM (students within teachers within schools, controlling for random-assignment blocks, baseline achievement, and student background) is already the standardized impact d = 0.058 in SD units. g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.9939 (df = n_clusters - 2 = 124). g_se = J*SE(d) with SE(d)=0.030; g_var = g_se^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Exhibit J.26 (p. J-22); also Exhibit 3.12 (p. 73) and Exhibit ES.5 (p. ES-14/15)
effect_sizes.notes: End-of-treatment (cumulative two-year) impact; the immediate post for the 2-year program. Not statistically significant (p=0.055); similar magnitude to the significant Year-1 estimate. Year-2 model controls for baseline-year achievement (two years prior). A sensitivity model controlling for prior achievement in BOTH subjects makes this Year-2 math estimate statistically significant (Exhibit J.32/33); the headline model (J.26) is reported here.
